readMe:
THIS FILE IS STEP 1 OF tools/loop/ITERATION-PROMPT.md AND IT MUST STAY READABLE IN ONE Read.
The Read tool has TWO ceilings: it TRUNCATES past ~25,000 tokens (~59 KB of this prose) and FAILS
outright past ~256 KB. BOTH HAVE ALREADY BITTEN. iter127 hit the byte ceiling - the Read was
refused, 459 KB, because the `done` log had reached 397 KB of it. iter128 found the TOKEN cap had
been truncating for longer and unnoticed: at 74,115 bytes / 31,303 tokens, step 1 returned lines
1-43 of 92 and silently dropped `decisions` (the six outstanding decisions), `doneCount`,
`doneArchive`, `doneRecent` and `spikes`. Truncation is the worse failure of the two because it
looks like success.

RUN `python3 tools/loop/check-state-size.py` AFTER EVERY EDIT TO THIS FILE. It prints the size, the
estimated token count, the largest fields and every other tools/loop file, and exits non-zero when
the file stops fitting. WHEN IT TRIPS: move an append-heavy field into an archive under tools/loop/
and leave a short pointer behind. There are six precedents - `doneArchive`, `blockersArchive`,
`gatesArchive`, `methodNotes`, `scratchInventory`, `spikesArchive` - and each one asserted its round-trip before this file was
rewritten. Do not discard content to make the check pass.

AND NOTE WHY THIS PARAGRAPH IS AT THE TOP OF THE FILE RATHER THAN NEXT TO `doneArchive`: a
truncated Read still shows it. iter127's rotation rule was correct and had no effect, because it
was written into a field that sat past the cut. A rule that keeps a file readable is worthless in
the half that gets cut off.
phase:
M6 feature-complete. NO GATE IS TICKED, SO THERE IS STILL NO FEATURE WORK THE LOOP MAY DO — and iter128,
like iter127, spent its increment on the loop's own machinery, found the same way: by obeying step 1 and
measuring what it actually returned.

  (1) STEP 1 WAS STILL BROKEN AFTER ITER127 FIXED IT, AND THE FIX'S OWN INSTRUCTIONS SAT IN THE HALF THAT
      GOT CUT OFF. iter127 split `done` out because state.json had crossed the Read tool's 256 KB BYTE
      ceiling (459 KB; the Read was refused outright). That was real and it worked. But the Read has a
      SECOND ceiling nobody had measured — a 25,000-TOKEN cap — and the 74 KB file was over it. `Read
      tools/loop/state.json` came back "PARTIAL view — showing lines 1-43 of 92 (31,303 tokens, cap
      25,000)", dropping `decisions` (ALL SIX OUTSTANDING DECISIONS, the largest field at 15 KB),
      `doneCount`, `doneArchive`, `doneRecent` and `spikes`. TRUNCATION IS THE WORSE OF THE TWO FAILURES
      BECAUSE IT LOOKS LIKE SUCCESS — a cold session gets a well-formed half-file and no error. And
      `doneArchive.howToAppend`, the rotation rule iter127 wrote to stop exactly this, sat at line 54.

  (2) FIXED AND MEASURED AT EVERY STEP: 74,115 bytes -> ~45 KB / ~19,600 tokens / 99 lines, and a LITERAL
      re-run of step 1 returns the whole file in one call (verified after the final write, not before).
      Seven extractions over two passes (.mtk/paths-128/split-state.py, split-state-2.py), each verbatim
      with its round-trip asserted before the live file was rewritten and NOTHING discarded. The newest
      `doneRecent` entry names all seven and why each one moved; the pointer fields at the foot of this
      file say where each landed and when to read it.

  (3) THE RULE NOW LIVES WHERE A TRUNCATED READ STILL SHOWS IT. That is the whole lesson of the iteration:
      iter127's rotation rule was CORRECT AND HAD NO EFFECT, because it was written into a field past the
      cut. `readMe` is now the 7th key, ahead of everything long, and `python3
      tools/loop/check-state-size.py` is a real check rather than prose — it prints size/tokens/largest
      fields, flags every other tools/loop file, and EXITS NON-ZERO when the file stops fitting (it exits 0
      today at ~19,600 of a 20,000-token budget, leaving ~11 KB of headroom).

  (4) THE TREE IS GREEN AND THE SANDBOX IS UNCHANGED. `dotnet build` 0 warnings / 0 errors; `dotnet test`
      1361/1361 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (34 s). DOCUMESBX re-probed read-only: 44 pages, version
      histogram {1: 43, 2: 1} with `Documentation Status` the only v2, and 9 of the 12 DocuMe pages
      carrying an accurate `stale` label. Identical to iters 125, 126 and 127 — nothing drifted, nothing
      was published, nothing was re-marked.

  (5) THE ITER120 SINGLE FAILURE DID NOT RECUR. Sixth clean full run in a row.

  (6) THE PHONE-PUSH CHANNEL IS STILL DEAD AND THE PROTOCOL STILL DOES NOT KNOW IT. iter126 recorded the
      tool answering "Mobile push not sent (Remote Control inactive)", so every gate/blocker push from an
      unattended session most likely went nowhere, while tools/loop/README.md advertises the phone channel
      as live. NOTHING REACHES MIRKO'S PHONE UNTIL A REMOTE-CONTROL SESSION IS CONNECTED; the Mac
      notification centre and this state file are the only channels that work unattended. Keep calling
      PushNotification (it costs nothing and starts working the moment Remote Control is on), but do not
      count a stalled loop as "reported".

the full instructions are in GATES.md. A ticked box is the only thing that turns this loop back into a
working loop. Cheapest first: gate-m3 (add one `approved` label), gate-m4 (write one wrong comment),
gate-m5 (answer decisions.m5Acceptance), gate-m2 (walk the 44 pages), gate-m6 (push main, then tag v0.1.0).

and report what does not work.** iter126 found the dead phone-push channel that way; iter127 found step 1's
Read failing on the byte ceiling; iter128 found it STILL failing on the token cap, which iter127's own fix
had not measured. THE BOUNDARY, and hold it: this licence covers the loop's own machinery — the files the

blockers: OPEN, ITER121, PHRASED AS A QUESTION — **may the loop push to origin/main?** WHAT I NEED: a value in `tools/loop/state.json → decisions.pushPolicy` — "always", "on-request" or "never". WHAT THE FACT IS: origin/main is at 699c855 ("iter74"); local main is at iter120; `git status -sb` reads [ahead 93] against a remote ref fetched the same day. The loop has never pushed in 120 iterations and no earlier iteration recorded it. Nothing is lost — every commit is on this machine. WHY I DID NOT JUST DO IT: 93 commits landing on Moberg's org fires ci.yml (push to main), is outward-facing, and is unfixable without the history rewrite §8.2 forbids; no gate or protocol line authorises it. WHAT I DO ONCE IT IS SET: "always" — push at the end of each iteration that commits, starting with the 93; "on-request" — push only when a gate needs the remote and say so; "never" — stop raising it, and gate-m6 keeps its 'push main by hand before you tag' step. THIS IS NOT BLOCKING ANY OFFLINE WORK; it blocks the remote-dependent half of gate-m5-refresh-roundtrip and makes gate-m6's tag step misleading if unanswered. AS OF ITER128 THE COUNT IS [ahead 104], not the 93 recorded above; the question and every consequence are otherwise unchanged.

decisions.mermaidDialectGap:
OPEN — FOR MIRKO, RECORDED ITER113, BLOCKS NO MILESTONE. beautiful-mermaid 1.1.3 (pinned in
package.json) renders `flowchart LR` and `sequenceDiagram` but REJECTS `graph TD;` and `pie`.
The `graph TD;` rejection is caused by the TRAILING SEMICOLON ALONE — `graph TD` renders fine.
Measured one dialect per run at .mtk/paths-113/probe-mermaid-dialects.py; re-runnable in ~30s.
OPTIONS AS WRITTEN INTO GATES.md: (a) upgrade or replace the renderer; (b) strip a trailing `;`
from the header inside tools/render-mermaid.mjs — one line, buys back `graph TD;`, does nothing
for `pie`, and quietly rewrites the user's diagram source; (c) accept both as known-unsupported
dialects and have the converter report them as a NAMED DEGRADATION instead of failing the page.
WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE GOLDEN CASE: this is PLAN.md §7's deferred question ('how many of the 59
AurServices mermaid diagrams does beautiful-mermaid reject?') arriving at M2 instead of M7, on a
corpus small enough to reason about. Whoever implements the answer should re-run the probe first.

Where does M5's §14 acceptance run? iter121 completed its live middle (deploy-sim -> stale label, done against DOCUMESBX; see gate-m5-refresh-roundtrip). The ends still need a repo with pull requests and, for the refresh half, secrets. OPTIONS: (a) install templates/workflows/docs-drift-pr.yml into .github/workflows/ on THIS repo and open one PR — cheapest, needs no secrets at all, and demonstrates the drift comment; (b) additionally add ANTHROPIC_API_KEY + DOCUME_CONFLUENCE_EMAIL/TOKEN as repo secrets and install docs-refresh.yml + docs-publish.yml, which demonstrates the whole chain but makes every push to main publish to the sandbox; (c) fold the acceptance into M7 Aur adoption, where a real repo with real PRs and a real deploy already exists, and reword the §14 criterion to say so. NOTE THIS INTERACTS WITH decisions.pushPolicy: a pull request on this repo presupposes the branch is on GitHub, and origin/main is 93 commits behind.
decisions.pushPolicy: OPEN — FOR MIRKO, RECORDED ITER121. Should the loop `git push origin main` as part of an iteration? TODAY IT DOES NOT AND NEVER HAS: origin/main is at 699c855 ("iter74") while local main is at iter120, i.e. [ahead 93]. The protocol says commit, not push, and the loop read that literally. WHY IT WAS NOT DONE UNILATERALLY AT ITER121: 93 commits arriving on Moberg's org fires ci.yml (it triggers on push to main), is visible to anyone watching the repo, and cannot be undone without the history rewrite rule §8.2 forbids. WHAT IT COSTS TO LEAVE: gate-m6's release instructions had to gain a 'push main first' step (a tag push carries its own objects, so the release would build from the tag while the default branch still showed iter74), and M5's PR-based acceptance is not reachable at all until the branch is on GitHub. ANSWER HERE: 'always' (loop pushes every iteration), 'on-request', or 'never' (and then expect to push by hand before each gate that needs the remote).
decisions.planSection6Deviations:
OPEN — FOR MIRKO, RECORDED ITER122, BLOCKS NO MILESTONE. PLAN.md §6's preamble says: "Global:
`--config <path>` (default `./docume.json`), `--verbose`, `--json` (machine output)". Measured against
every command's own `--help` at iter122, that sentence is false in three ways, and each needs a direction
rather than a guess:
  (a) `--verbose` IS BUILT NOWHERE. No command takes it and nothing in the repo records a decision to
      drop it. Building it is not mechanical — it means deciding what a verbose run says, across the
      Spectre output and the Confluence client.
  (b) `--json` IS BUILT ON `status` ALONE (StatusCommand.cs). `drift` spells its machine output
      `--format table|json|github-comment` instead, which §6.4 specifies and which covers the same need
      under another name. `init`, `publish`, `sync`, `dashboard` and `convert` have no machine output.
  (c) `--config` IS ABSENT FROM `init` AND `convert`. Both are defensible — `init` writes docume.json in
      the working directory rather than being pointed at one, `convert` takes the wiki root as an argument
      plus `--renderer` — but §6 says global without excepting them.
THE TWO DIRECTIONS: (1) BUILD the missing flags (three slices, (a) the largest); or (2) CORRECT §6's
preamble to say what actually shipped and why (`--json` where a machine consumer exists, `--config` where
there is a config to resolve), which is a spec edit and therefore yours.
WHERE TO PUT THE ANSWER: this field. WHAT I DO THEN: implement it, and STRIKE THE ENTRY OFF
`UnbuiltOptions` in tests/DocuMe.Core.Tests/Acceptance/PlanCommandSpecTests.cs — that test fails if a
listed gap is built, so the record cannot drift from reality in either direction.
WHY I DID NOT PICK ONE: rewriting the spec to match the code is how a spec stops being a spec, and §4.3's
rule against regenerating a golden to make a test pass is the same rule one level up. The gap is now
visible and asserted, which is the part that was missing.
decisions.planSection5Deviations:
OPEN — FOR MIRKO, RECORDED ITER123, BLOCKS NO MILESTONE. PLAN.md §5.1 declares two config fields that
LOAD, VALIDATE, ROUND-TRIP AND ARE READ BY NO LINE OF src/. A consumer can set either and nothing at all
happens. Each needs a direction rather than a guess:

  (a) `links.repoBlobUrl`. §5.1 declares it ("optional: linkify source refs at baseline SHA"), §6.2 step 2
      SPECIFIES THE BEHAVIOUR ("linkify source refs to `repoBlobUrl@baselineSha` if configured"), and
      plugin/skills/docs-loop/SKILL.md:169 TELLS THE SKILL IT WORKS: "If `docume.json` sets
      `links.repoBlobUrl`, publish linkifies those refs at the baseline sha". A shipped skill asserting a
      behaviour the CLI does not have is why this is worse than iter122's unbuilt flag. OPTIONS: build the
      linkification in the publish path (it is a converter/link-map concern — §6.2 step 2 sits right next
      to the relative-link rewrite that IS built), or strike the promise from §6.2, from the skill and
      from §5.1.
  (b) `drift.defaultBranch`. §5.1 declares it (default "dev") and §10's PR bullet writes `docume drift
      --baseline origin/<defaultBranch>`. No command reads it. templates/workflows/docs-drift-pr.yml
      deliberately computes a MERGE BASE from the pull request instead (its comment even says "that
      setting is for local runs"), and a local `drift` with no --baseline falls back to state.json's
      baselineSha — so the local case does not read it either. OPTIONS: have the no---baseline fallback
      consult it (`origin/<defaultBranch>` before baselineSha, or as the documented default), or drop the
      field from §5.1 and stop §10 implying a branch default exists.

WHERE TO PUT THE ANSWER: this field. WHAT HAPPENS THEN: the loop builds or removes as instructed, and IN
THE SAME SLICE strikes the entry off `DeadFields` in
tests/DocuMe.Core.Tests/Acceptance/PlanDataContractTests.cs and deletes its bullet from
docs/wiki/20-reference/configuration.md's "Two fields are inert in this version" section. The test fails
from BOTH sides if only one of those happens, which is deliberate.

WHY THE LOOP DID NOT PICK: rule §4.3 says never regenerate a golden to make a test pass; choosing between
"build the feature" and "delete the promise" is the same rule one level up. iter122 set this precedent for
planSection6Deviations and it holds here.
decisions.planSection9Deviation: OPEN, ITER124, PHRASED AS A QUESTION — may PLAN.md §9's CI-posture bullet and rule §1.5 be reworded? THE FACT: both say feedback processing runs with "read-only repo access + PR-only writes". No GitHub job can have read-only repo access AND open a PR from a branch — pushing docs/feedback-<date> needs `contents: write`, and templates/workflows/docs-feedback.yml grants exactly that (contents: write + pull-requests: write) with a comment at the permissions block saying why. Nothing is mis-built: the job never pushes to the default branch and holds no Confluence credentials at all, and docs/wiki/30-automation/workflows.md ALREADY words it correctly ("none of them pushes to the default branch"). So the plan and the rule are the wrong two, and no consumer-facing page needs touching. WHAT I NEED: a yes/no here, or a rewording. WHERE: this field. WHAT I'LL DO WITH IT — on yes, edit PLAN.md §9's bullet to the wiki's wording and strike the entry off `PlanDeviations` in tests/DocuMe.Core.Tests/Acceptance/PlanSemanticsTraceTests.cs; .claude/rules/security.md §1.5 needs YOUR paste, same class as the paste-rule-8-2a blocker, because the loop cannot write .claude/. On no, the entry stays and the deviation is a recorded, tested-for choice rather than an oversight.
decisions.planSection10Deviations: OPEN, ITER125, TWO ENTRIES, BOTH PROSE-ONLY AND BOTH IN PLAN.md (which the loop CAN edit — it did not, for the same reason iter123 and iter124 did not: picking a direction on the spec is Mirko's, not the loop's). (a) THE ONE THAT MATTERS, because it settles half of planSection5Deviations at the same time. §10's second bullet spells the PR job as `docume drift --baseline origin/<defaultBranch> --format github-comment`. templates/workflows/docs-drift-pr.yml passes `git merge-base "origin/<the PR's base ref>" HEAD` instead, and its comment says why: diffing against the base branch TIP attributes every commit merged into the base since the branch started to this PR, so the comment lists pages the author never touched. THE TEMPLATE IS RIGHT AND THE BULLET IS WRONG. And this bullet is THE ONLY PLACE IN THE PLAN that gives `drift.defaultBranch` a job — the dead knob iter123 found in §5.1. So correcting §10 here either kills that config field outright or forces the question of what else would read it. WHAT I NEED: a direction, in this field. Step 1 of the iteration protocol is "Read tools/loop/state.json"; that Read has been failing — 459,395 bytes against the Read tool's 256 KB ceiling — so every cold session was falling back to ad-hoc python just to orient, and a session that did not think to fall back would have oriented on nothing. NOTHING WAS DISCARDED: .mtk/paths-127/split-done.py asserted the round-trip before rewriting the live file (list equality, canonical-JSON equality, and 1..N contiguous numbering — 127/127) and .mtk/paths-127/state-before-split.json is the pre-split copy. Verified no consumer breaks: nothing parses tools/loop/state.json in C#, shell, yml, mjs or py (only `cat` in docume-loop.sh's comments and log lines), so no test asserts its shape; build 0 warnings/0 errors and dotnet test 1361/1361 after the split. THE ROTATION RULE IS NOW WRITTEN INTO THE FILE ITSELF (doneArchive.howToAppend): append one archive line at n = doneCount + 1, bump doneCount, push onto doneRecent, TRIM doneRecent to 5.
